title: Laws, duties, deadlines and remedies
author: LcudkPQzLuuqsnzHSmJ7iLREaHStvPKRVb
status: Unsigned AI-assisted reference; no independent legal review
scope: Shared reference for unsupported rent acceleration and connected collection, reporting, recording and court-process questions; imported legal sources from other current Commons subjects

rules.title: Mitigation after abandonment
rules.applies_to: Landlord of the leased premises; identify the legally responsible owner/lessor.
rules.trigger: Abandonment in breach of a lease.
rules.deadline: Duty concerns reasonable efforts during the relevant vacancy period; this section specifies no 30-day response deadline for a records request.
rules.required_action: Take reasonable steps to reduce avoidable rental loss; a purported waiver of the duty is void.
rules.consequence: Failure to mitigate can reduce recoverable loss to the extent it reasonably could have been avoided.
rules.limits: A missing answer does not itself prove no mitigation occurred. The lease, events, efforts and avoidable amount require evidence.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Security deposits and a distinct 30-day rule
rules.applies_to: Residential landlord as defined by §92.001(2); a management agent is not automatically that landlord.
rules.trigger: Surrender of possession and the written forwarding-address condition in §92.107.
rules.deadline: Generally refund within 30 days after surrender; the refund/itemization obligation is conditioned on the written forwarding address.
rules.required_action: Refund the deposit or account for lawful deductions, subject to statutory exceptions.
rules.consequence: §92.109 provides bad-faith presumptions, deposit remedies and specified forfeitures; §92.109(b) addresses suit for damages to the premises.
rules.limits: This is not a blanket 30-day deadline to prove accelerated rent or an automatic forfeiture of every lease claim.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Creditor, collector and third-party collector
rules.applies_to: Persons directly or indirectly engaged in consumer debt collection, including qualifying original creditors.
rules.trigger: The entity’s actual conduct and role in collecting an alleged consumer debt.
rules.deadline: Definition; no response clock.
rules.required_action: Distinguish the broad Texas debt-collector definition from the narrower third-party definition.
rules.consequence: Determines which provisions and duties may apply.
rules.limits: Texas location alone does not make every entity a third-party collector; federal FDCPA coverage is a separate question.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Written disputes and the 30-day statement
rules.applies_to: Covered third-party debt collectors; determine the actual collector separately from the source creditor or property manager.
rules.trigger: Receipt by that collector of qualifying written notice identifying an inaccuracy in its file.
rules.deadline: Written statement no later than day 30 after receipt. Admitted inaccuracies: correction within five business days.
rules.required_action: Investigate and send a statement admitting or denying the inaccuracy, or explaining insufficient investigation time. Collection must cease as provided in (a). The insufficient-time route requires interim file changes, recipient notices and cessation under (d).
rules.consequence: On completion notify the consumer. Under (e), a determination of accuracy permits reporting and collection to resume. Civil remedies are addressed by §392.403.
rules.limits: A denial is not an obligation to send every requested document. Missing the response deadline does not automatically erase the underlying lease debt; a later investigation does not make an earlier response timely.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Unauthorized incidental charges
rules.applies_to: Covered Texas debt collectors.
rules.trigger: Attempt to collect interest or an incidental charge, fee or expense.
rules.deadline: Conduct rule; no general reply deadline.
rules.required_action: Collect those amounts only when expressly authorized by the agreement or legally chargeable.
rules.consequence: A proven violation can support applicable Chapter 392 remedies.
rules.limits: A disputed fee is not automatically unauthorized; identify the governing provision and facts.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: False amounts and deceptive collection
rules.applies_to: Covered Texas debt collectors, potentially including the source creditor’s own collection conduct.
rules.trigger: A qualifying misrepresentation or deceptive means in collection.
rules.deadline: Conduct rule; no general reply deadline.
rules.required_action: Avoid misrepresenting the character, extent or amount of a consumer debt and other prohibited deception.
rules.consequence: A proven violation can support applicable Chapter 392 remedies.
rules.limits: Silence alone does not establish that every charge was false; connect the communication, inaccuracy and applicable legal elements.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Federal coverage and creditor exclusions
rules.applies_to: Qualifying federal debt collectors and consumer debts.
rules.trigger: Actual business, ownership, collection and acquisition circumstances.
rules.deadline: Definition; no response clock.
rules.required_action: Determine coverage independently for each defendant.
rules.consequence: Controls availability of FDCPA claims.
rules.limits: An original creditor or qualifying manager may be excluded federally while remaining subject to other law.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Validation period and collection pause
rules.applies_to: Covered debt collector receiving a timely written dispute.
rules.trigger: Written dispute submitted within the validation period, generally 30 days after validation information is received.
rules.deadline: 30 days is principally the consumer’s dispute period. This provision sets no fixed number of days for the collector to provide verification.
rules.required_action: Stop collecting the disputed portion pending the required verification response; Regulation F recognizes a portal that accepts consumer communications.
rules.consequence: Collection can resume after compliant verification; stopping indefinitely is different from responding within a fixed deadline.
rules.limits: Do not substitute this rule for Texas §392.202. Verification is not necessarily disclosure of every document needed to litigate the merits.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Portal submissions and duplicative disputes
rules.applies_to: Covered debt collectors and timely written consumer disputes.
rules.trigger: Use of a medium through which the collector accepts consumer communications.
rules.deadline: Validation-period conditions apply; no daily-upload entitlement or automatic new deadline.
rules.required_action: Apply the written-dispute and collection-pause rules. Duplicative treatment has conditions, including prior compliant verification and absence of new material information.
rules.consequence: A compliant verification or duplicative-dispute response can permit resumption under the rule.
rules.limits: A portal submission to the creditor is not automatically receipt by the collector; preserve the recipient and exact submission.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: False balances, disputed status and unauthorized amounts
rules.applies_to: Covered federal debt collectors.
rules.trigger: Collection representations, credit communications and amounts sought.
rules.deadline: Conduct rules; no general response clock.
rules.required_action: Avoid false debt representations; communicate known disputed status; collect amounts authorized by agreement or law.
rules.consequence: Proven violations can support §1692k remedies.
rules.limits: A failure to send requested records and a false or unauthorized amount are distinct propositions to prove.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Represented consumers
rules.applies_to: Covered collectors who know the consumer is represented about the debt and know or can readily ascertain counsel’s name/address.
rules.trigger: Knowledge of representation, subject to statutory exceptions.
rules.deadline: Ongoing communication restriction.
rules.required_action: Generally communicate through counsel.
rules.consequence: A prohibited direct communication may support an FDCPA claim.
rules.limits: Does not guarantee the attorney access to a particular company officer or reviewer.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Bureau reinvestigation and results
rules.applies_to: Consumer reporting agencies.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a qualifying dispute by the bureau.
rules.deadline: Generally 30 days; up to 15 additional days for qualifying relevant information during that period. Results generally within five business days after completion; procedure description within 15 days after request under (7).
rules.required_action: Reinvestigate reasonably, forward relevant information, consider relevant consumer material, and correct/delete/modify as the statute requires.
rules.consequence: Inaccurate, incomplete or unverifiable information requires appropriate correction or deletion; qualifying violations may support civil claims.
rules.limits: The bureau’s clock is not automatically triggered by a letter delivered only to the source creditor or property manager. Deletion from a report does not itself extinguish a contractual debt.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Reasonable accuracy procedures
rules.applies_to: Consumer reporting agencies preparing consumer reports.
rules.trigger: Preparation of a consumer report.
rules.deadline: Ongoing procedure duty.
rules.required_action: Follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy.
rules.consequence: Qualifying failures and harm can support applicable FCRA remedies.
rules.limits: A bureau’s repeated balance is not independent evidence of the underlying lease calculation.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Furnisher duties and private-claim boundaries
rules.applies_to: The entity furnishing information to a consumer reporting agency; do not automatically assign that role to the property manager.
rules.trigger: For (b), notice from a bureau under §1681i(a)(2); direct disputes and known inaccuracies implicate different provisions.
rules.deadline: The (b) investigation must finish within the applicable bureau investigation period.
rules.required_action: Investigate, review relevant bureau-supplied material, report results and make required corrections. (a)(3) addresses disputed-status reporting.
rules.consequence: Privately enforceable investigation claims generally arise under (b); (c)–(d) restrict private enforcement of (a), including its regulations.
rules.limits: Sending documents directly to the collector or source creditor does not by itself establish the bureau-notice trigger for a (b) damages claim.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Direct disputes to furnishers
rules.applies_to: The actual furnisher receiving a qualifying direct dispute at a specified or otherwise qualifying address.
rules.trigger: Receipt of an adequately identified account, disputed information, explanation and supporting material, subject to exceptions.
rules.deadline: Generally the applicable §1681i investigation period; frivolous/irrelevant determination notice within five business days of determination.
rules.required_action: Investigate reasonably, consider relevant supplied material, report results to the consumer and correct inaccurate furnishing.
rules.consequence: A regulatory duty exists; private damages enforcement must be analyzed with §1681s–2(c)–(d).
rules.limits: No automatic email receipt is specified here. A new upload is not automatically a fresh independent investigation duty.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Texas collection remedies
rules.applies_to: Persons with an actionable Chapter 392 violation and the required injury or basis for relief.
rules.trigger: Proof of a covered violation and the remedy’s conditions.
rules.deadline: No general response clock in these provisions.
rules.required_action: §392.403 permits injunctions, actual damages caused by violations, and fees/costs for a successful action; (e) provides at least $100 for successful specified violations including §392.202. §392.404 links Chapter 392 violations to DTPA remedies.
rules.consequence: Possible recovery is not confined to the federal FDCPA additional-damages ceiling.
rules.limits: The $100 provision is not for every Chapter 392 violation. DTPA requirements, defenses and damages rules still require analysis.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Deceptive-practices remedies
rules.applies_to: Qualifying consumers and actionable practices; consider statutory definitions, exclusions and any tie-in claim.
rules.trigger: A covered practice causing the required harm, with additional findings for enhanced damages.
rules.deadline: Remedy provision; see §17.505 for notice.
rules.required_action: Establish the applicable claim, causation and damages. Knowing or intentional conduct can support enhanced damages under the specified rules.
rules.consequence: Economic damages, qualifying mental-anguish damages, fees and potentially up to treble damages, depending on findings and claim.
rules.limits: A demand amount is not itself the plaintiff’s actual loss. Enhanced damages are not automatic or interchangeable with common-law punitive damages.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: DTPA pre-suit notice
rules.applies_to: Consumer contemplating a covered damages suit and the intended defendant.
rules.trigger: Notice reasonably detailing the complaint, damages and reasonably incurred expenses, including attorney fees if any.
rules.deadline: Generally at least 60 days before filing; statutory exceptions apply.
rules.required_action: Give the required written notice and particulars.
rules.consequence: Noncompliance can lead to abatement while notice is supplied and the period runs.
rules.limits: This is a claimant’s pre-suit requirement, not 60 days for a creditor to prove the debt. An ordinary follow-up email is not automatically a compliant notice.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: FDCPA damages, fees and filing period
rules.applies_to: Each plaintiff with a viable FDCPA claim against a covered collector.
rules.trigger: A proven violation of that plaintiff’s rights; separate proof is needed for each person.
rules.deadline: Generally file within one year of the violation under (d); tolling issues require specific analysis.
rules.required_action: Prove the claim and any actual damages caused. Additional individual statutory damages are discretionary up to $1,000 per action; successful actions can recover reasonable fees/costs.
rules.consequence: Two qualifying plaintiffs can each receive an award. Multiple calls do not each generate $1,000.
rules.limits: Do not automatically multiply awards by defendants acting together for the same injury. §1692k has no separate punitive-damages award; other claims may have other remedies.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Willful and negligent FCRA noncompliance
rules.applies_to: A defendant violating a privately enforceable FCRA requirement and a plaintiff with a viable claim.
rules.trigger: Willful or negligent noncompliance, as applicable.
rules.deadline: See §1681p for filing limits.
rules.required_action: Prove the actionable duty, violation, required injury/causation and culpability.
rules.consequence: Willful: actual damages or $100–$1,000 statutory damages, possible punitive damages and fees/costs. Negligent: actual damages and fees/costs.
rules.limits: These are not automatic amounts per letter or per defendant. A direct-dispute regulatory breach alone does not establish private FCRA liability.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: FCRA filing period
rules.applies_to: Persons bringing FCRA civil actions.
rules.trigger: Discovery of the violation and occurrence of the violation.
rules.deadline: Earlier of two years after discovery or five years after occurrence.
rules.required_action: Identify each claim’s dates and any applicable exceptions.
rules.consequence: A late lawsuit can be time-barred.
rules.limits: A follow-up letter or company investigation does not automatically restart a filing period.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Federal participant recording
rules.applies_to: Private participants in a wire, oral or electronic communication.
rules.trigger: A participant recording, or one participant’s prior consent.
rules.deadline: Consent relates to the recording when made.
rules.required_action: Federal law generally permits participant recording, subject to the criminal-or-tortious-purpose exception.
rules.consequence: State recording laws can add restrictions.
rules.limits: A company’s own recording notice is not automatically permission for every other recording or publication.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: New Mexico telephone recording
rules.applies_to: Participants in telephone communications involving New Mexico.
rules.trigger: Consent of a sender or intended recipient.
rules.deadline: Consent concerns the recording when made.
rules.required_action: Generally one-party consent for a participant’s telephone recording.
rules.consequence: Potential recording-law liability if recording is unlawful.
rules.limits: Interstate facts and other participants’ actual locations matter; a corporate address does not establish an employee’s location.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Georgia participant audio recording
rules.applies_to: Participants in communications involving Georgia.
rules.trigger: The person recording is a participant, or a participant gives prior consent.
rules.deadline: Consent concerns the recording when made.
rules.required_action: Generally permits participant audio recording.
rules.consequence: Assess any other applicable jurisdiction independently.
rules.limits: The audio rule does not create blanket permission for private video surveillance or recording court proceedings.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Discovery scope
rules.applies_to: Litigants in federal civil proceedings.
rules.trigger: A pending case and the particular discovery or testimony request.
rules.deadline: Case orders and the rule determine timing.
rules.required_action: Discovery must concern relevant, nonprivileged material and be proportional to the case.
rules.consequence: Court orders can enforce or limit properly presented requests.
rules.limits: A plan to subpoena everyone is not automatically proper.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Depositions and organizational witnesses
rules.applies_to: Litigants in federal civil proceedings.
rules.trigger: A pending case and the particular discovery or testimony request.
rules.deadline: Case orders and the rule determine timing.
rules.required_action: Parties may agree, or a court may order, remote depositions. Under (b)(6), an organization must designate and prepare witnesses on reasonably particularized topics.
rules.consequence: Court orders can enforce or limit properly presented requests.
rules.limits: An informal call is not a deposition; applicable notice, oath, recording and discovery rules remain.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Remote trial testimony
rules.applies_to: Litigants in federal civil proceedings.
rules.trigger: A pending case and the particular discovery or testimony request.
rules.deadline: Case orders and the rule determine timing.
rules.required_action: Remote testimony requires the applicable good-cause/compelling-circumstances showing and safeguards under (a).
rules.consequence: Court orders can enforce or limit properly presented requests.
rules.limits: A preference for Zoom does not guarantee a remote hearing or trial.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Subpoenas
rules.applies_to: Litigants in federal civil proceedings.
rules.trigger: A pending case and the particular discovery or testimony request.
rules.deadline: Case orders and the rule determine timing.
rules.required_action: Attendance and production subpoenas have service, geographic, burden and objection limits.
rules.consequence: Court orders can enforce or limit properly presented requests.
rules.limits: Remote technology does not automatically eliminate subpoena restrictions.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Admissions, defaults and justice-court distinctions
rules.applies_to: Parties in the Texas court and proceeding governed by the specific rule.
rules.trigger: A pleading, formal discovery request, failure to answer or failure to attend, as specified.
rules.deadline: Rule-specific; a private demand letter is not formal requests for admissions.
rules.required_action: Use the applicable procedural response and identify what is actually admitted or established.
rules.consequence: Defaults and deemed admissions can have legal consequences under their own conditions.
rules.limits: Do not import district-court rules automatically into justice court or treat unanswered ordinary correspondence as a judicial admission.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Party statements and business-record foundations
rules.applies_to: Evidence offered in a proceeding where these rules apply.
rules.trigger: An offered statement or business record and its foundation.
rules.deadline: Applicable filing/service and court rules determine timing.
rules.required_action: Establish relevance, authenticity and the applicable evidentiary basis.
rules.consequence: Qualifying statements or records may be admitted.
rules.limits: A digital signature does not independently prove every charge; a record maker need not always personally testify.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Referral, mediation and confidentiality
rules.applies_to: Parties in covered dispute-resolution proceedings.
rules.trigger: A court referral or covered mediation communication.
rules.deadline: Orders and statutory provisions control.
rules.required_action: Distinguish attendance requirements from agreement to settle and assess confidentiality.
rules.consequence: Objections and confidentiality rules have their own consequences.
rules.limits: A recollection about mediation does not alone establish judicial misconduct or the disposition of a case.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

rules.title: Amicus briefs
rules.applies_to: Proposed amici in federal appellate proceedings.
rules.trigger: A proposed amicus filing in a specific appeal.
rules.deadline: Rule and court-specific filing requirements.
rules.required_action: Meet applicable permission/consent, disclosure, timing and form requirements.
rules.consequence: The court determines acceptance.
rules.limits: Publishing a Commons article does not make it an accepted amicus brief or establish trial-court admissibility.
rules.review_status: Primary text reviewed; no independent legal review

case_law.scope: Reasonable reletting efforts; failure to mitigate as an affirmative defense and proof of avoidable loss. The linked 2026 opinion is a commercial-lease application; it is not a ruling in the author’s case.

case_law.citation: Horton Brothers damages opinion, D. Del., No. 02-1656 (2007)
case_law.scope: Awarded a separate $1,000 to each qualifying plaintiff. Shared account status does not automatically establish each person’s claim.

case_law.citation: Kearney v. Salomon Smith Barney, 39 Cal.4th 95 (2006)
case_law.scope: Illustrates interstate recording choice-of-law analysis; not a ruling that California governs a New Mexico–Georgia call.
